ledger.claim: The distance driven on this trip is measured on the GPS trace, not on the receipt: EV-GPS-00108 carries 206 fixes at a 10-second sample interval with 100% coverage and no gaps, and its trace_distance_km of 26.17 governs over the rounded 26.2 km carried on the trip record, which POL-RD-01 says may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: there is no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds.

On the platform's own derived deviation facts this trip ran 5.17 km, or 24.6%, beyond the optimal route - above both the 0.8 km absolute floor and the 20% proportion, so a route deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(b) is discharged.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03's exoneration cannot be run on this record and the driver's bare assertion that he drove 'exactly where the app told me' is an assertion citing no evidence ID that carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The only rider instruction on the chat log is a request to change the destination terminal to T3 ('sorry ah can change to T3?', sent 07:41:40); no message names a road and no message carries a waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 excludes nothing for the rider and the two loops of the T3 departure kerb the driver admits making are not conduct the rider requested or should pay for.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, and the fare model is METERED: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read off the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee and 0 ERP/tolls on the optimal route = 27.63. The refund is 33.77 charged_total - 27.63 = 6.14, payable 6.15 after rounding up. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and 18.2% of the amount charged, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND, not FULL_REFUND.

The rider has carried the POL-RD-08 initial burden on identity: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00108 and the same 07:19:20 start, so the burden shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause and cannot discharge it with a general assertion that he drove as directed.

The rider's profile does not trigger any corroboration requirement: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so this claim may not be discounted on profile grounds; and under POL-GEN-01 no other field on either profile - rating, account age, lifetime counts - may ground a finding against the rider.

ledger.claim: Both endpoints of this trip were amended after booking: the pickup was moved to Punggol MRT at 07:12:30 (pickup_amended_at) and the dropoff was changed to Changi T3 at 07:41:52 (dropoff_amended_at). Under POL-RD-05 the POL-RD-01 threshold must therefore be re-applied against the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints, which the record stores as amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 km and amended_optimal_duration_min 31.0 - not the 21.0 km booked Rivervale-to-T1 figure the rider is comparing against.

Measured against the governing amended optimal of 24.60 km, the trace distance of 26.17 km yields an excess of only 1.57 km, which is 6.4% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km; the 6.4% share fails the first limb, so the establishment test fails, no deviation exists, and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which POL-RD-01 makes mandatory over trip_record.actual_distance_km.

The rider's complaint that 'I have taken this exact trip many times and it is 21 km' uses the BOOKED optimal for the original Blk 118 Rivervale Drive to Changi Terminal 1 itinerary. POL-RD-05 provides that distance driven to conform to an amended endpoint is never counted as excess against the driver, and the platform itself re-quoted the amended route at 24.60 km at 07:41 - the rider is comparing the receipt against a route she replaced.

The chat log shows both amendments were the rider's own instructions: at 07:11:58 she wrote 'im at punggol mrt phv pickup bay instead, moved the pin', and at 07:41:40 'sorry ah can change to T3? my friend flight is T3 not T1'. POL-RD-05 expressly names, among the amendments that reset the baseline, a rider moving the pin and 'a terminal change from T1 to T3' - which is precisely what happened here.

The rider's second complaint - 'he drove around the airport for another five minutes' - is also answered by POL-RD-05, which excludes distance where the rider was not at the amended point and the trace shows the vehicle circling within 400 m of it for more than 4 minutes. The driver's on-file statement is that the rider was not at the T3 kerb and he 'went round the loop twice looking for her'; the rider's own claim puts that circling at five minutes; and the trace records two loops of the T3 departure kerb within 380 m of the amended pin. The zone-dependent derived.arrival block is unavailable here because trip_record.pickup_zone_class is null, so the duration rests on the parties' own recorded accounts rather than a computed dwell - but on either account the circling is excluded.

Even taken on the platform's own numbers there is no MATERIAL deviation: an excess of 1.57 km on 24.60 km is neither greater than 50% of optimal nor greater than 8.0 km absolute, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not triggered at all. In any event the driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 402, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists under either limb of POL-RD-06.

The refund figure of 6.15 (refund_before_rounding 6.14) carried in the fare breakdown is only generated on the premise that a deviation was established against the booked 21.0 km optimal. Because POL-RD-05 substitutes the 24.60 km amended baseline and no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, the condition for POL-RD-02 is not met, that recomputation never runs, and no distance-or-time refund is due.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The artifacts match on trip_id and pickup timestamp and the trace is unimpaired, but the excess measured from that trace against the governing amended baseline is 6.4%, below the POL-RD-01 threshold - so the burden never shifts to the driver and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

There is no independent billing-integrity route to a refund either. The fare is METERED and reconciles to the cent: the 0.00 airport surcharge is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, and no ERP gantries were charged, so POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line to correct and the $33.77 charge stands.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING, has no payload, and carries weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. The driver advances no external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is not in play on either side and the absent advisory decides nothing - the case turns on POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-01 alone.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The $33.77 charge stands and no refund is due.

Why. This trip was re-routed twice by the rider after booking, and POL-RD-05 governs how the deviation test is run. The rider moved the pickup from Blk 118 Rivervale Drive to Punggol MRT (chat 07:11:58 'im at punggol mrt phv pickup bay instead, moved the pin'; pickup amended 07:12:30) and changed the destination from Changi T1 to Changi T3 (chat 07:41:40 'sorry ah can change to T3?'; drop-off amended 07:41:52). POL-RD-05 names both a rider moving the pin and a T1-to-T3 terminal change, and it requires the POL-RD-01 test to be re-run against the optimal route between the amended endpoints — the stored amended_optimal_distance_km of 24.60 km (amended_optimal_duration_min 31.0), which the Judge may not re-derive.

The measurement. The GPS trace is unimpaired — 206 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, so POL-RD-07 does not bite — and its trace_distance_km of 26.17 km governs over the rounded 26.2 km on the receipt. Against the amended 24.60 km baseline the excess is 1.57 km, or 6.4% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is BOTH above 20% of optimal and above 0.8 km; 6.4% fails the proportion limb, so no deviation is established and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

The rider's figures. The rider's comparison against 21.0 km is the booked Rivervale-to-T1 estimate that her own two amendments replaced; it is not the governing baseline, and the derived 5.17 km / 24.6% excess in the GPS block is measured against that superseded figure. The rider's 'five minutes driving around the airport' is the two loops of the T3 departure kerb the trace shows within 380 m of the amended pin; the rider was not at the kerb, and POL-RD-05 excludes that circling from excess in any event.

Money. The fare reconciles to the cent: 3.80 base + 19.65 distance + 9.52 time + 0.80 platform fee = 33.77. The 0.00 airport surcharge is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, and no ERP gantry was charged, so there is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). POL-RD-02 — the recomputation and the 6.15 refund the rider asks for — runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01; none is, so it does not run.

Claims answered. RIDER: the trace-integrity claim (EV-GPS-00108) is accepted and the trace is policy-clean under POL-RD-07; the 5.17 km / 24.6% deviation claim is rejected because POL-RD-05 substitutes the 24.60 km amended baseline, which leaves 1.57 km / 6.4%; the 6.15 POL-RD-02 refund claim falls with it; the POL-RD-04 point (a terminal change is not a named road or waypoint) is accepted and excludes nothing; the POL-RD-08 identity claim is accepted (all three artifacts carry TRP-00108 and the 07:19:20 start) but the rider has not shown limb (b), an excess meeting the threshold; the profile claim is accepted and no corroboration requirement arises (deviation_claims_60d is 1). DRIVER: the POL-RD-05 claim, the 1.57 km / 6.4% computation, the booked-optimal point, the chat-amendment point, the circling-exclusion point, the POL-RD-06 no-pattern point (deviation_flags_90d 0 of 402 completed trips in 90 days), the POL-RD-02-not-applicable point, the POL-RD-09 point and the POL-RD-03/missing-advisory point are all accepted.

No referral. No conduct referral fires under POL-RD-06(c) — no repeat-deviation pattern exists. No billing-integrity referral fires under POL-RD-09(4) — no phantom charge line. No traffic advisory was on file and none was needed; an uncited external cause carries no weight (POL-RD-13, POL-RD-08), and the case does not escalate because the trace is clean and the identifiers match.

Confidence 0.9, above the 0.70 floor; the deciding facts rest on the trip record and the GPS trace, both at full weight 1.0. The monetary effect is $0.00, below the $8.00 execution threshold. This differs from precedents P-0001 and P-0002 (PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-RD-01/02/08) because there the booked optimal governed, whereas here the rider's own endpoint amendments move the baseline to 24.60 km and leave the excess below the POL-RD-01 threshold.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
